THE HERO'S Y DOES NOT SURVIVE SUSPEND/RESTORE AT A MEGAPROJECT SITE (F-1095-1) -- the first bug the restored suite caught, invisible for nine days because its spec could not collect until rf-33 (e3db39ae) landed. e2e/restore-validation.spec.ts:656 fails on BOTH projects DETERMINISTICALLY with root.hero.position.y: 0.14559222393281415 != 0.2763519114255905, and the differences array has EXACTLY ONE entry. Everything the test is named for passes (normalized, restored, targetActive, targetId all true/correct); only exact flips false. The compared sides are the snapshot the game was TOLD to restore versus the state it actually ended up in, so restore is not reproducing the Y it was handed, and the spec's own exact:true assertion is the already-ratified contract. tasks.note_s1172: Authored s1172 2026-07-28 from F-1170-4 (BACKLOG:25) - the DRAINED REFUTATION of the previous attempt - plus F-1160-2 (BACKLOG:208) and its s1161 re-derivation. This is the third and last cheap mechanism on this finding: BOTH published remedies are dead (min-of-3 refuted s1161 at 4/4 under systematic deprioritisation; in-process reference loop refuted s1170 with bands disjoint, ref inflated 3.12x vs the solve 6.11x), and any in-process CPU PROXY inherits that refutation, so this task builds no proxy and no environment model - it changes what the guard SAYS and how many consecutive over-caps the runner REQUIRES. PREMISES RE-DERIVED AT SOURCE BEFORE AUTHORING, not inherited: run-guards.mjs is 74 lines with NO retry of any kind and exits 1 if any row is non-zero (:62,:74); check-power-graph-budget.mjs emits the p95 on BOTH paths but in two different formats, one of them inside the assert message (:40-43 vs :44), which is why every handoff records a BOOLEAN for a measurement that produced a NUMBER; test:guards is the sole caller (package.json:20); and NO test for run-guards.mjs exists among the twelve scripts/*.test.mjs files, so a retry policy added there would be the first untested branch inside the very file built because a gate is its exit code and not its printed counter. THE MEASURE-FIRST STOP (scope 1) targets the assumption the remedy silently makes - that two consecutive fresh-subprocess runs are INDEPENDENT. The banked data is openly suggestive of clustering: under sustained taskpolicy -b the failures are 100% correlated (s1161 12/12, s1170 6/6). Critically the master FORBIDS answering this by counting rare over-cap events (at a pooled 5/52 ~ 9.6% that estimates a conditional from three or four events - the same dead end that made s1160's stated gate unrunnable) and requires the LAG-1 AUTOCORRELATION OF THE CONTINUOUS p95 SERIES instead, n>=40 ordered and timestamped, with |r| >= 0.3 STOPPING the retry half as a declared full success. TWO CORRECTIONS s1172 MADE TO F-1170-4's OWN WORDING: (1) the finding's remedy is guard-agnostic, but a blind retry across all eight would apply flake-tolerance to seven deterministic contract checks (test:task-guards gates the ledger, test:deploy-contract gates the deploy shape) and would MASK a genuinely intermittent contract break - a worse defect than the one being fixed - so the retry is an ALLOWLIST OF ONE with a named constant and a measured justification; (2) the reporting half (scope 2) is UNCONDITIONAL and ships even if scope 1 stops the retry, because it has zero dependence on the independence assumption. Scope 4 carries TWO mutation controls because the task adds two ways to swallow a red: a genuine cost regression injected into the SUBJECT (PowerGraph.ts, reverted, git diff main -- src/ empty as a gated deliverable) proving a double failure still reds, AND an allowlist control proving a non-allowlisted guard still reds on its FIRST failure with no second run. A retried pass must print FLAKED, never PASS - a flake nobody can see is how this guard gets trained out through the other door. The 0.5ms cap is FIREWALLED (a budget edited to fit its measurement is not a guard). The four e2e specs lane-a holds live this hour are firewalled by name (Mistake #12).

tasks.authorNotes: PREMISE AND CURE BOTH MEASURED BY THE AUTHORING FIRE, NOT PROPOSED FROM THEORY. Three arms, same machine, same session: pre-merge main (13 files, spawnSync) 72 tests 0/6 red; merged (15 files, spawnSync) 74 tests 4/11 red; merged + prototype cure 74 tests 0/8 red. Every failure is whole suite collects without loading Vite-only modules, twice directly and twice nested inside the new meta-guard. Mechanism verified at the captured bytes: the failing assertion is assert.match(result.stdout, /Total: [1-9]\d* tests/) while result.status is 0 and the listing is well-formed — the capture is simply truncated before the trailing Total: line. Full solo capture 296,028 bytes; failing captures ~153,474 chars (ending mid-line at assay-ledger-page.spec.ts:80:1) and ~156,216 chars. TWO DIFFERENT TRUNCATION POINTS = A RACE, NOT A BOUNDARY, and NOT maxBuffer (296 KB is under the 1 MB default, and overflow would set ENOBUFS + null status). Four concurrent execFile listings return the full 296,028 bytes every time, so the defect follows the SYNCHRONOUS capture. THE OLD GREEN WAS A FALSE GREEN — the meta-guard did not create the race, it exposed it, so do NOT cure this by lightening the battery, and the meta-guard is explicitly OUT of firewall as the detector rather than the fault. ANTI-SCOPE: neither /Total: [1-9]\d* tests/ regex may be touched — both are correct and were already refuted as a phantom defect in s1201 (F-1201-1); this would be the second run to cure a regex that was never broken. The observe-first gate is scope 1 and warns that a QUIET MACHINE CAN HIDE A LOAD-DEPENDENT RACE, so 8/8 green is not a STOP by itself — re-run under load, and proceed to scope 2 regardless because the truncation mechanism is verified independently of the flake rate.

tasks.drainNotes: s1210. ACCEPTED, AND IT IS BETTER THAN ITS OWN REPORT CLAIMED. The cure moves the control loop INSIDE the page — one page.evaluate dispatches keydown then samples __THREE_GAME_DIAGNOSTICS__ every 16ms in-browser, releasing on a speed-aware lead (speed/28 + 0.08) and resolving only once the hero has actually stopped — so accuracy no longer depends on round-trip latency, which is exactly the mechanism s1207 measured (166-491ms against an intended 25ms loop). The outer loop re-picks the dominant axis over up to 12 attempts and converges on hypot(dx,dz)<=0.12 instead of per-axis inequalities, curing the 'one pass per axis, never re-check x after z' defect; it also dismisses a levelup overlay that could eat the movement. GATES: tsc 0 · build green 1.38s · e2e/release-build.spec.ts under its REAL config 24/26. Runner's retained numbers: approach failures 5/8 (62.5%) -> 0/8, 72/72 movements converged, and a MUTATION CONTROL (12 attempts -> 3) restored 6/8 — a guard shown failing, not only passing. TEST-ONLY SLICE, no src/ touched. Base 4fdbc950 is an ancestor of main and `git diff 4fdbc950 main` on both paths is EMPTY, so both files applied clean with no 3-way. ⚠️ F-1210-5: the 2 residual failures at release-build.spec.ts:21 are NOT this slice's — they are GG-01b's, proved by a one-variable control this fire (cure + GG-01b = 2/2 FAIL on 'town-open-board not visible'; cure - GG-01b = 2/2 PASS in 57.9s). The runner's honest 'inventory remains red' note therefore under-credits its own cure. ⚠️ F-1210-6 (mine, disclosed): this slice landed as an UNLABELLED SWEEP inside 0b8db8f9 — `git checkout c162bd1a -- <paths>` stages what it writes, and a later plain `git commit` took the whole index, so a commit whose message names only GG-01b ledger work also carries this cure. Content correct and fully gated; the message is wrong, and this review is the correction. HARNESS LESSON WORTH THE LEDGER: e2e/release-build.spec.ts runs ONLY under playwright.release.config.ts (vite preview on 5190). Run under the default dev config it fails 10/10 including 'dist has no later manifest ids', a test no graft could affect — a red inherits its harness config.
